meta.face: A Frisian of about sixty-five with a pale, fair complexion and a LONG, OBLONG head — a very HIGH, smooth forehead running up into a tonsured crown with a thin ring of short white hair, very SMALL, pale-blue eyes set CLOSE together under faint fair brows, a LONG, THIN, straight nose, LARGE, PROTRUDING EARS, a long, clean-shaven upper lip over a SMALL, PRIM, closed mouth, a small, rounded chin; CLEAN-SHAVEN; the gaze inward and steady, a little lowered.
meta.basis: No likeness from life; Wikipedia's lead image and the Vita Secunda miniature (German Wikipedia) show a mitred bishop without individual features. Wikipedia: 'represented either as a bishop holding a church and a book or as standing between two geese'; German Wikipedia: the goose attribute since the seventeenth century, from the geese he drove off. The book tells his schooling under Alcuin at York, his priestly labours, his founding of Werden, his see of Münster and his answer to Charlemagne. The long head with small close-set eyes and large ears is our choice. No mitre: the miniatures give him one, but the card shows him bare-headed with his tonsure.
